title: Photosynthesis: How Plants Make Food
description: How a leaf turns sunlight, water and air into food, and why it matters.
subject: Biology

cards.title: Plants cook their own food
cards.body:
A leaf uses **sunlight** to turn **water** and **carbon dioxide** into **glucose**, a sugar the plant lives on.

**Oxygen** is the leftover from this cooking, and it escapes into the air.

cards.question: Which gas leaves the leaf during photosynthesis?
cards.explanation: Oxygen is released when water is split, and it exits through tiny pores in the leaf.

cards.text: In photosynthesis, a leaf takes in ___ and gives off ___ into the air.
cards.explanation: Carbon dioxide goes in, oxygen comes out.

cards.question: In which part of the cell does photosynthesis happen?
cards.explanation: Chloroplasts hold the chlorophyll, which is why they’re called the cell’s kitchen.

cards.prompt: In what order do the steps of photosynthesis happen?
items: Water splits and oxygen is released
Light energy is stored in ATP
cards.explanation: The first three are the light reactions. The last happens in the Calvin cycle, which uses the stored energy to turn CO₂ into glucose.

cards.title: Why leaves look green
cards.body:
Chlorophyll is the green pigment inside chloroplasts. It soaks up **red** and **blue** light and uses that energy.

Green light isn’t absorbed well, so it bounces back to our eyes. That’s why leaves look green.
cards.note: Leaves look green because chlorophyll reflects green light.

cards.text: To absorb light, a leaf needs the green pigment ___.
cards.explanation: Chlorophyll captures light energy for photosynthesis.

cards.question: Which colors of light does chlorophyll absorb best?
cards.explanation: Red and blue are absorbed; green is mostly reflected.

cards.title: What happens in low light?
cards.body:
Photosynthesis runs on light energy. The more light a leaf gets, the more glucose it makes and the more oxygen bubbles it gives off.

But past a certain point, more light stops helping. Something else, like the amount of CO₂, becomes the limit.

cards.question: A plant already gets lots of light. What happens if you add even more?
cards.explanation: Past a point, another factor like CO₂ or temperature limits the rate.

cards.title: From the soil to the leaf
cards.body:
Root hairs soak up water from the soil. It travels up the stem through thin tubes called **xylem**, then spreads through the leaf’s veins to every cell.

Carbon dioxide takes a different route: it enters through tiny pores on the leaf called **stomata**.

cards.prompt: How does water from the soil reach the chloroplasts?
items: Root hairs absorb water from the soil
It rises up the stem through the xylem
Leaf veins carry it to the cells
Light energy splits it in the chloroplasts

cards.question: Where does carbon dioxide enter the leaf?
cards.explanation: Stomata open to let CO₂ in and oxygen and water vapor out.

cards.text: Tiny pores on a leaf are called ___.
cards.explanation: One pore is a stoma; many are stomata.
